unharnessed.meaning: Every rule survives: "TDY travel is longer than 12 hours and needs a pre-approved authorisation in Concur.", "If you leave GSA, any unused travel comp time is lost."
unharnessed.sense: The plain swaps fit: "getting to and from work" for commuting, "runs out" for expires, "work out" for calculate.
unharnessed.authenticity: Reads as natural Australian workplace English: "Please get in touch with your Timekeeper", "Once you hit the expiry date, you lose the leave."
unharnessed.register: A shade under level 2: Australian spelling and plain phrasing ("Have a look", "check out") but almost no slang.
unharnessed.tone: Keeps the plain policy tone: "Travel comp time hours are based on elapsed time."
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly: "Travelling during your usual work day counts as regular hours, including getting to the airport from home."
unharnessed.variety: Little slang to vary; "work out" carries three of the calculations ("work out the breakdown", "For working out", "to work out elapsed time").

yarn-troppo.meaning: The rules survive, but it invents examples of what counts as gap-filler time: "Think sitting at the gate, or stuck in a plane seat with your knees up round your ears." In a policy page that reads as guidance the original never gives. Other asides ("Sorry, the commute doesn't count.", "So use it or lose it.") restate the original.
yarn-troppo.sense: "Here's the go", "put in for", "Sing out", "tallying up" fit; "No fiddling with the clocks." implies a rule about cheating where the original only says which time zone to use.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Natural idiom ("Here's the go:", "Sing out to your Timekeeper"), with stock tags bolted on: "That's what they're there for.", "simple as that", "Now, the catch."
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than level 2: a yarn opener, a tag line after most paragraphs ("Everyone's in.", "No fiddling with the clocks."). No swearing.
yarn-troppo.tone: The plain policy tone turns chatty and jokey: "Sorry, the commute doesn't count.", "with your knees up round your ears".
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads easily, though the stream of tags breaks up the instructions.
yarn-troppo.variety: Varied: "Here's the go", "put in for", "trek", "squiz", "nitty-gritty", "Sing out", "tallying up", "use it or lose it".
yarn-troppo.essence: Still the policy page in shape, but recast as a friendly pep talk: "Now, the catch."

engine.meaning: The original word for word, so every rule survives.
engine.sense: No Aussie terms to misfire; only spellings change ("authorisation", "Travelling").
engine.authenticity: No Australian voice at all, and US officialese left in: "When you reach the expiration date, you will forfeit the leave."
engine.register: Untranslated apart from spelling; nowhere near a level 2 light touch.
engine.variety: No slang at all to vary.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every rule survives: "TDY travel runs more than 12 hours", "If you leave GSA, any unused travel comp time is forfeited."
yarn-dinkum.sense: "There's no cap", "Have a squiz", "sing out to your Timekeeper" fit their contexts.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural Australian workplace English: "If you've got questions, sing out to your Timekeeper or an HR Specialist at your agency."
yarn-dinkum.register: Light level 2 touch: "no cap", "squiz", "sing out", otherwise plain. No swearing.
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads smoothly: "Travelling during your usual work day counts as regular hours, and that includes getting from home to the airport."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied for its size: "no cap", "squiz", "sing out", "runs out"; "work out" recurs.

dinkum-3.meaning: Every rule survives, reordered without loss: "Anyone can earn travel comp time: there are no limits based on salary level or schedule type."
dinkum-3.sense: "put in for", "have a squiz" fit; "Give your Timekeeper ... a shout" works, though in Australia "shout" also means buying a round.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Natural Australian workplace English: "If you're current GSA staff and want more detail".
dinkum-3.register: Light level 2 touch: "put in for", "squiz", "a shout". No swearing.
dinkum-3.flow: Reads smoothly: "The hours are based on elapsed time, and you work that out using the time zone you left from."
dinkum-3.variety: Varied for its size: "put in for", "squiz", "a shout", "As a rule", "runs out".

unharnessed.why: Plain rewording with no Aussie colour; the text sits a little under the brief throughout.

unharnessed.quote: Use the time zone where you departed from
unharnessed.original: Use the time zone at departure
unharnessed.why: 'Where you departed from' is a slightly clumsy double preposition.

yarn-troppo.quote: Think sitting at the gate, or stuck in a plane seat with your knees up round your ears.
yarn-troppo.why: Invented examples of what qualifies, in a policy document.
Added aside implying a rule the original doesn't state.
Added quip; part of the over-weighting and tone shift.

engine.quote: You may request travel comp time when you are approved to travel for work
engine.original: You may request travel comp time when you are approved to travel for work
engine.why: Left untranslated; the brief is not attempted.

yarn-dinkum.quote: Use the time zone where you left from
yarn-dinkum.original: Use the time zone at departure

dinkum-3.quote: Give your Timekeeper or an HR Specialist at your agency a shout.
dinkum-3.original: Please contact your Timekeeper or an HR Specialist at your agency
dinkum-3.why: 'A shout' can read as shouting someone a drink; mild ambiguity.

summaries.unharnessed: Plain, natural and faithful; a touch lighter than the brief.
summaries.yarn-troppo: Lively and varied but over the brief, chatty in tone, with invented policy examples.
summaries.engine: The original with spelling changes; fails the brief.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: Light, natural and faithful; right on the brief.
summaries.dinkum-3: Light, natural and faithful; right on the brief.
